conventions: Supplied relative pronoun: read what the relative stands over. An articleless attributive participle takes it into its own unit under rule 41's closing sentence (35.10 נֹתֵן → *Who giveth*; 35.11 מַלְּפֵנוּ → *Who teacheth*), but a relative the ASV writes over a finite clause juxtaposed to a written antecedent answers to no morpheme and is `added` under rule 55 (35.5 שְׁחָקִים גָּבְהוּ מִמֶּךָּ → *the skies which are higher than thou*). The chapter writes both shapes within six verses; the morphology of the predicate word is what decides, not the English.

Supplied English verb in a verbless clause whose predicate is a preposition: a copula, a *to be* frame or a relational verb joins that preposition's unit under rules 20 and 49 (35.2 לְמִשְׁפָּט → *to be*, headed on *to*; 35.14 לְפָנָיו → *is before*), but a full lexical event verb is `added` under rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause and leaves the preposition `unrepresented` under rule 40 (35.8 לְאִישׁ ... לְבֶן־אָדָם → *may hurt* ... *may profit*, both italic). The subtraction test is what separates them: *hurt* and *profit* introduce an event the Hebrew never predicates, whereas dropping *to be* or *is before* removes only the link English writes for a predication the Hebrew already made. Four of this chapter's six BSB disagreements ride on this line.

Comparative מִן takes *more than* headed on *than* where the ASV writes a separate degree word (35.2, 35.3, 35.11 first), and a bare *than* where the English adjective already carries the comparison (35.5 *higher*, 35.11 second *wiser*). Count the degree words the ASV wrote rather than reading the construction off the Hebrew; 35.11 writes both shapes in one verse. Where the comparative phrase is the predicate of a verbless clause it also carries the construction-supplied copula under rule 49, as 35.2 מֵאֵל → *is more than God's* does.

Rule-30 fusions of a preposition with its construct noun or negative substantive were left with the status each verse pass returned: מִפְּנֵי → *Because of* is `aligned` (35.12) while לְפָנָיו → *is before* (35.14) and בִּבְלִי → *without* (35.16) are `noncompositional`. Edges and heads are identical under either status, and the corpus uses both in quantity for these same expressions, so nothing in the contract or precedent prefers one. This is recorded so a later reader does not mistake it for a split and re-open it.
report: Checked all 18 candidate lemma groups plus every `added` unit, which the table is blind to, reading the dump end to end. No cross-verse split found; patches empty.

Supplied relative pronouns were the closest call and are licensed by morphology rather than drift: *Who* stays with the articleless attributive participles נֹתֵן (35.10) and מַלְּפֵנוּ (35.11) under rule 41's closing sentence, while the *which* of 35.5 stands over a finite verb (גָּבְהוּ) with a written antecedent (שְׁחָקִים), which rule 46 excludes in its own terms and rule 55 marks `added`. Adjacent verses, opposite treatments, correct both times.

Supplied English verbs are divided on rule 20's own boundary and are consistent chapter-wide: a copular or result frame goes to the preposition that is the verbless clause's predicate (35.2 לְ → *to be*; 35.14 לְפָנָיו → *is before*), while the lexical event verbs *may hurt* and *may profit* (35.8) predicate an event the Hebrew never wrote, so they are `added` and both לְs go `unrepresented` under rule 40. This is the chapter's one genuinely contested call; the verse pass named the competing rule-49 reading, and the ASV italics corroborate without deciding, by rule 7.

Every lemma pair that looks like a disagreement is ASV-driven. לְ + 3ms suffix: *unto* (35.6), nothing (35.7, bare indirect object *givest thou him*, rule 40), *for* (35.14). לֹא: *none* where the ASV recasts the negation onto the subject nominal (35.10, 35.12), *not* where it does not (35.13, 35.14). בְּ and הַ: written in 35.10, unwritten in 35.15, where פַּשׁ is promoted to the direct object of *regard*. מִן: *of* in 35.7 (ablative), *by reason of* in 35.9 (causal). כִּי: *That* in 35.3, *when* in 35.14. The two waws of 35.1 are two morphemes, and rule 14's list is read off the ASV.

Connectives count out correctly against the morphemes present: the italic *Or* (35.2) and *And* (35.3) are `added` because no conjunction stands in either clause, while the written אוֹ of 35.7 takes its *Or* and every waw takes the word written for it. The two אִםs are consistent too: 35.6 gives both *If*s to the one written אִם under rule 55's closing paragraph, leaving its waw only *And*; 35.7 has one אִם and one *If*.

Comparative מִן is uniform once the degree word is counted: *more than* headed on *than* where the ASV writes a separate *more* (35.2, 35.3, 35.11a), a bare *than* where the English adjective already carries the degree (35.5 *higher*, 35.11b *wiser*). Rule 24's ruling that the head is *than* and not the degree adverb holds in all five.

The two construct chains of 35.11 are placed by counting which word each *the* stands before, per rule 29: בַּהֲמוֹת אָרֶץ has no article morpheme and takes two supplied *the*s (rules 29 and 15), while עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם is rule 29's arthrous case, the article taking the *the* before its own word and the construct a supplied one. Nothing is fronted in either.

One cosmetic inconsistency, left alone: the chapter marks מִפְּנֵי → *Because of* `aligned` (35.12) beside לְפָנָיו → *is before* and בִּבְלִי → *without* `noncompositional` (35.14, 35.16). No edge or head differs between the two statuses, and the corpus uses both in quantity for these exact expressions (לִפְנֵי → *before*: 424 aligned, 266 noncompositional; מִן+פָּנֶה → *because of*: 59 aligned, 23 noncompositional), so neither the contract nor precedent prefers one. Forcing uniformity would be a change with no basis; recorded as a convention instead.

BSB disagreements: all six are the documented convention difference, none a genuine error. 35.2 הֲ is unrepresented because the ASV marks the question by inversion alone (*Thinkest thou*), which rule 17 settles. 35.4 מִלִּין is unrepresented because the ASV writes no *words* in that line. 35.7 לְ, 35.15 בַּ and the two לְs of 35.8 are rule 40 recastings where BSB attaches the preposition to its phrase. The 35.8 pair is the only one where BSB's reading matches a materially defensible alternative, and that alternative is already named in the verse's review notes.

No promotions or amendments. The chapter's three general judgments — the relative-pronoun line, the supplied-verb line, and the comparative degree count — are each an application of rules 41/46/55, 20/49 and 24 as written, not a gap in them. The one thing the contract does not cover, 35.3's recasting of the single nominal מֵחַטָּאתִי as *more than if I had sinned* with a supplied *if*, rests on one hedged instance with no corpus support in the packet, and a rule built on that would be worse than none.
